blocks.text: B1-18 · Listening to simplified news
Lesson overview

The radio news is the first authentic text that can be followed by ear: it is read in Arabic standard by a conductor who articulates well, has a fixed structure, repeats the main news (titles at the beginning, details after) and uses a few dozen passing formulas. In this unity learn how a news report is made, the formulas that hold it together ( ⁧عَلَى صَعِيدٍ آخَرَ⁩ , ⁧فِي سِيَاقٍ مُتَّصِلٍ⁩ , ⁧أَفَادَ مُرَاسِلُنَا⁩ ), to hear numbers, dates and names said quickly, and a technique of listening in three steps. The news of the unit are simplified and invented; In the last part you start listening to real news (see Appendix C), knowing that at first you will understand the headlines. Two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 133–134), plus the EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, voice synthesis scripts or tutor, a recorder (also the phone), Appendix C for authentic news
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. to recognise the parts of a newsletter and the formulas which introduce them;
2. to understand who is the source of news ( ⁧أَفَادَ⁩ , ⁧نَقَلَ عَنْ⁩ , ⁧ذَكَرَتْ مَصَادِرُ⁩ ) and use correctly ⁧إِنَّ⁩ after ⁧قَالَ⁩ and ⁧أَنَّ⁩ after other verbs;
3. Listen to a simplified news in three steps and fill out the grid "Chi," what, where, when, because it does not work;
4. understand numbers, percentages, dates and temperatures at normal speeds;
5. write and read a one-minute news report aloud.
Two-week plan.

blocks.text: 1. Dialogue 1 · I only understood the numbers
Before class. Luca listened to an Arabic radio news in the car.

rows: ⁧لُوكَا: أُسْتَاذَةُ، اِسْتَمَعْتُ أَمْسِ إِلَى نَشْرَةِ أَخْبَارٍ عَرَبِيَّةٍ فِي السَّيَّارَةِ. فَهِمْتُ الأَرْقَامَ فَقَطْ!⁩
Professor, yesterday I listened to an Arabic news in the car. All I know is the numbers!
⁧سَلْمَى: هٰذِهِ بِدَايَةٌ جَيِّدَةٌ. وَمَاذَا كَانَتِ الأَرْقَامُ؟⁩
Salmā: It's a good start. And what were the numbers?
⁧سَلْمَى: الدَّرَجَاتُ فِي الطَّقْسِ، طَبْعًا. وَالنِّسْبَةُ؟ هَلْ تَذْكُرُ كَلِمَةً قَبْلَهَا؟⁩
Salmā: Degrees were in the weather, of course. And the percentage? Do you remember a word before?
⁧؟ لَا أَعْرِفُ. كَانَ المُذِيعُ سَرِيعًا⁩ « ⁧البِطَالَة⁩ » ⁧؟ أَوْ⁩ « ⁧التَّضَخُّم⁩ » … ⁧أَظُنُّ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧جِدًّا.⁩
Luke: I think... ♪ Inflation ♪? Or unemployment? I don't know. The speaker was very fast.
⁧سَلْمَى: المُشْكِلَةُ أَنَّكَ اسْتَمَعْتَ مَرَّةً وَاحِدَةً، وَأَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَفْهَمَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ.⁩
Salmā: The problem is that you only listened once and wanted to understand everything.
Luke: So what do I have to do?

⁧سَلْمَى: اِسْتَمِعْ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ. فِي المَرَّةِ الأُولَى، المَوَاضِيعُ فَقَطْ: سِيَاسَةٌ؟ اِقْتِصَادٌ؟ رِيَاضَةٌ؟ فِي الثَّانِيَةِ: مَنْ؟ مَاذَا؟ أَيْنَ؟ مَتَى؟ وَفِي الثَّالِثَةِ: الأَرْقَامُ وَالتَّفَاصِيلُ.⁩
SalmāListen three times. The first time only the topics: politics? economy? Sports? The second: who? What? Where? When? And the third: numbers and details.
But the radio doesn't repeat the news!
⁧سَلْمَى: النَّشْرَاتُ مَوْجُودَةٌ عَلَى الإِنْتِرْنِت، تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ تُعِيدَهَا كَمَا تُرِيدُ. وَالعَنَاوِينُ فِي البِدَايَةِ تُسَاعِدُكَ: المُذِيعُ يَقُولُ لَكَ مُسْبَقًا مَا سَتَسْمَعُ.⁩
Salmā: The news is on the internet, you can listen to it as much as you want. And the titles help you at first: the speaker tells you in advance what you will hear.
Luke: As if he gave me the solution before the exercise!
⁧سَلْمَى: بِالضَّبْطِ. وَبَعْدَ أُسْبُوعَيْنِ سَتَعْرِفُ أَيْضًا الكَلِمَاتِ الَّتِي تَرْبِطُ الأَخْبَارَ بَعْضَهَا بِبَعْضٍ.⁩
Salmā: Exactly. And in two weeks, you'll also know the words that connect the news to each other.

blocks.text: What to notice. ⁧المُذِيع⁩ The speaker, the conductor ( ⁧أَذَاعَ⁩ • to transmit • to transmit). ⁧مُسْبَقًا⁩ In advance, the following information shall be provided: ⁧يُعِيدُ⁩ Replay, send back on the air (IV of ⁧ع و د⁩ ). ⁧كَأَنَّهُ⁩ ... as if.......... ⁧بَعْضَهَا بِبَعْضٍ⁩ • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • The technique of the three listenings is the section 5.
2. The structure of the news

rows: Here radio... · Welcome to the news
Here are the main titles · Let's start with the titles
our correspondent at... · is with us on the phone...
And in sports... · And finally the weather
That concludes our news · Thank you for listening

blocks.text: News arrives in order of importance: first domestic and foreign politics, then the economy and society, then sport, finally the weather. Every news begins with the sentence-synthesis (who did what, where, when); The details come later. If you lose the first sentence, you have lost the news: that's why the initial titles are precious.
3. The formulas of passage

rows: change of topic: ... move on to more ...
new address book: ⁧وَفِي الاِقْتِصَادِ⁩ In economic terms
background information: ... it was remembered that ...
final addition:         • it must be said that... • •

blocks.text: … ⁧نَعُودُ إِلَى⁩ return to previous news

These formulas are your road sign: when you hear ⁧عَلَى صَعِيدٍ آخَرَ⁩ you know that a new news begins and you can reset your attention; when you hear ⁧فِي سِيَاقٍ مُتَّصِلٍ⁩ You know the theme stays the same. ⁧يُذْكَرُ أَنَّ⁩ (Lett. "It's mentioned that ") often closes news with a fact of the past: ⁧يُذْكَرُ أَنَّ آخِرَ زِيَارَةٍ كَانَتْ قَبْلَ عَشْرِ سَنَوَاتٍ.⁩
4. The sources: who says so?

rows: … ⁧نَقَلَتْ وَكَالَةُ الأَنْبَاءِ عَنْ مَصْدَرٍ رَسْمِيٍّ أَنَّ⁩
The news agency reports, quoting an official source, that...
has confirmed · has specified · has added ... that...

blocks.text: … ⁧نَقْلًا عَنْ⁩ Quoting...

⁧إِنَّ⁩ or ⁧أَنَّ⁩ ? After ⁧قَالَ⁩ is used ⁧إِنَّ⁩ (with kasra), because it brings words back as a speech; after all other communication verbs ( ⁧أَفَادَ⁩ , ⁧ذَكَرَ⁩ , ⁧أَكَّدَ⁩ , ⁧أَعْلَنَ⁩ , ⁧أَوْضَحَ⁩ , ⁧أَضَافَ⁩ ) used ⁧أَنَّ⁩ . On the news, the difference is well: qāla inna... · afāda Anna... The source participle. Often the source follows the news with a participle to the accusative (ḥāl, B1-09): … ⁧مُشِيرًا إِلَى أَنَّ⁩ ... emphasising that it is ... ⁧مُؤَكِّدًا أَنَّ⁩ ...confirming that it is.
5. Listen in three steps
1. First listening: the arguments. Listen to everything without stopping. Just write the section of each news ( ⁧سِيَاسَة⁩ ,
⁧اِقْتِصَاد⁩ ...) and a keyword. Use the initial titles as a map.
2. Second listen: the grill. For each piece of news please fill: ⁧مَنْ؟⁩ chi · ⁧مَاذَا؟⁩ what · ⁧أَيْنَ؟⁩ where · ⁧مَتَى؟⁩ when ·
⁧لِمَاذَا؟⁩ Because. Stop after every word, not after every word.
3. Third listening: numbers and details. Now you can stop and listen to the sentences: numbers, names, quotes.

Before you listen: predict. Reading or hearing a title, write three words that you expect: for ⁧زِلْزَال⁩ You're expecting ⁧بِقُوَّةِ⁩ , ⁧ضَحَايَا⁩ , ⁧فِرَقُ الإِنْقَاذِ⁩ . The words are much easier to recognize. What not to do. Don't stop on a word you don't know: after two seconds you lost the following sentence. Don't translate while you listen. Don't start with the fastest authentic news: first use the drive scripts, then slow news or for students, finally the normal ones.
6. Dialogue 2 · Behind the microphone
Video call with Laylā Ḥaddād, which today led the radio news of its station.

rows: ⁧لُوكَا: لَيْلَى، سَمِعْتُكِ صَبَاحَ اليَوْمِ عَلَى الإِنْتِرْنِت! كُنْتِ أَنْتِ المُذِيعَةَ؟⁩
Luca: LaylāI heard you on the Internet this morning! Were you the host?
⁧لَيْلَى: نَعَمْ، زَمِيلِي كَانَ مَرِيضًا. قَرَأْتُ نَشْرَةَ الثَّامِنَةِ عَلَى الهَوَاءِ مُبَاشَرَةً.⁩
Laylā: Yes, my colleague was ill. I read the 8:00 news live.
⁧لُوكَا: كَيْفَ تَقْرَئِينَ بِهٰذِهِ السُّرْعَةِ وَبِلَا أَخْطَاءٍ؟⁩

⁧لَيْلَى: أَقْرَأُ النَّصَّ قَبْلَ البَثِّ مَرَّتَيْنِ، وَأَضَعُ الحَرَكَاتِ عَلَى الأَسْمَاءِ الصَّعْبَةِ وَعَلَى الأَرْقَامِ.⁩
Laylā: I read the text twice before transmission and put vowels on difficult names and numbers.

⁧لَيْلَى: المُحَرِّرُ الَّذِي يَكْتُبُ النَّشْرَةَ. هِيَ مِثْلُ الجُسُورِ بَيْنَ الأَخْبَارِ: تَقُولُ لِلْمُسْتَمِعِ إِنَّ خَبَرًا انْتَهَى وَخَبَرًا جَدِيدًا بَدَأَ.⁩
Laylā: The editor who writes the news. They are like bridges between the news: they tell the listener that one news is over and another news has begun.
And I use them as road signs!

⁧اِسْتَمِعْ إِلَى نَشْرَةِ المَسَاءِ، فَهِيَ تُكَرِّرُ⁩ : ⁧فِكْرَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ. وَنَصِيحَتِي⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ ⁧أَهَمَّ أَخْبَارِ الصَّبَاحِ. إِذَا سَمِعْتَ الخَبَرَ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي يَوْمٍ وَاحِدٍ، تَفْهَمُهُ⁩ ⁧أَحْسَنَ.⁩
Laylā: Nice idea. And my advice: listen to the evening news, which repeats the most important news in the morning. If you hear the same news twice in a day, you understand it better.

The air, directly in the air). ⁧البَثّ⁩ The transmission shall be the same as the transmission. ⁧يُشَكِّلُونَ⁩ Vocalize (II of ⁧ش ك ل⁩ , B1-17). ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ آلَافٍ⁩ or ⁧ثَلَاثَةَ آلَافٍ⁩ : desinence depends on the function in the sentence (subject or object); is the number one difficulty of reading the news aloud. ⁧العِبَارَات⁩ • the expressions • • • • • • • • • • • • • . • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • ⁧المُحَرِّر⁩ The editor is the editor. ⁧جُسُور⁩ pl. of ⁧جِسْر⁩ Bridge.
7. Numbers, dates and names by ear

Big numbers. On the news they feel whole: ⁧أَلْفَانِ وَخَمْسُمِئَةٍ⁩ 2.500 · ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ مَلَايِينَ⁩ 3.000.000 · ⁧مِلْيَارُ دُولَارٍ⁩ 1 billion dollars · ⁧نِصْفُ مِلْيُونٍ⁩ 500.000. Remember the order: thousands, hundreds, then units before tens ( ⁧خَمْسَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ⁩ = 25). Make it a habit to write the figures as you listen, from left to right, as you hear them: first the thousands, then the hundreds, then leave a place for the tens and write the units. The percentages and decimal places. ⁧خَمْسَةٌ فَاصِلَةُ سَبْعَةٍ بِالمِئَةِ⁩ 5,7% · ⁧رُبْعُ⁩ 1/4 · ⁧ثُلُثُ⁩ 1/3 · ⁧ضِعْفُ⁩ • the double • the double •. The dates. ⁧فِي الخَامِسِ عَشَرَ مِنَ الشَّهْرِ الجَارِي⁩ On 15 This month's ⁧مَطْلَعَ الشَّهْرِ المُقْبِلِ⁩ At the beginning of next month ⁧أَوَاخِرَ العَامِ⁩ At the end of the year. Names. Names of places and entities (ONO-03) often arrive in initial or short form: ⁧الأُمَمُ المُتَّحِدَةُ⁩ , ⁧الاِتِّحَادُ الأُورُوبِّيُّ⁩ , ⁧الجَامِعَةُ العَرَبِيَّةُ⁩ . Foreign names are adapted to Arabic phonetics: ⁧بَارِيس⁩ , ⁧رُومَا⁩ , ⁧مَدْرِيد⁩ , ⁧بُرُوكْسِل⁩ . If you don't recognize a name, write it down how you feel and look for it later.

9. Simplified and authentic news
The passage from the news of the course to the real ones is done in degrees.

rows: Scripts of this unit (B, C), read by tutor or vocal synthesis
The same scripts read faster; the headlines of a real news
the arguments and sentence-synthesis of each news

blocks.text: 3 A real short news bulletin (5 minutes), heard twice in the arguments, at least three news with the same full day grid

For the layer 3 use the public broadcasters listed in Appendix C. Choose short news, listen to them in the evening after reading the headlines of the same day on a news site: you will already know what we are talking about. Don't worry if at first you understand the 30–40%: it's normal, and the percentage rises fast if you listen every day.
10. Pronunciation

As a conductor reads. The conductor pronounces all the terminations within the sentence and stops in pause (without desinence) at the end: afāda murāsilunā anna l-wafda waṣala ṣabāḥa I-yawm. It imitates this rhythm: fast inside the group of words, small pause to the comma, longer break to the point. The tanwīn and numbers. The numbers have complete terminations: ṯalāṯatu ālāfin, ḫamsatan wa-ʿišrīna (indicative). Listening, don't let yourself be confused: ⁧الحَرَكَة⁩ final does not change the number. Shadowing. Listen to a phrase in Script B, stop, repeat it with the same rhythm and pitch. Then record the entire Script B and compare it to the original.

blocks.text: 13. Exercises
Exercise 1 · What is it for?

Match each formula with its function (opening of titles · switching to details · changing of topic · same topic · source · background information · last heading · closing): a) ⁧إليكم أهم العناوين⁩ · b) ⁧والآن إلى التفاصيل⁩ · c) ⁧على صعيد آخر⁩ · d) ⁧في سياق متصل⁩ · e) ⁧أفاد مراسلنا⁩ · f) ⁧يذكر أن⁩ · g) ⁧وأخيرا حالة الطقس⁩ · h) ⁧بهذا نصل⁩
⁧إلى ختام نشرتنا⁩

Complete with ⁧إِنَّ⁩ or ⁧أَنَّ⁩ and translate: a) ⁧قال الوزير ◌ المفاوضات مستمرة⁩ · b) ⁧أكد المدير ◌ المدرسة لن تغلق⁩ · c) ⁧ذكرت الوكالة ◌ الوفد وصل صباحا⁩ · d) ⁧وأضاف ◌ النتائج إيجابية⁩ · e) ⁧قالت المذيعة ◌ النشرة ستبث مساء⁩ · f) ⁧أعلنت البلدية ◌ الدخول مجاني⁩ · g) ⁧يذكر ◌ الاتفاق وقع قبل عامين⁩ · h) ⁧أفاد مراسلنا ◌ المباحثات انتهت إِيجَابِيّ⁩ .
